pr_title: Detect textures used in decals and light projectors as used in 3d

issue_context.title: Textures specified in an OmniLight3D or SpotLight3D projector are not detected as used in 3D
issue_context.body:
*Related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/62031.*

### Godot version

4.0.alpha (184709427)

### System information

Fedora 36, GeForce GTX 1080 (NVIDIA 510.68.02)

### Issue description

Unlike textures specified in a BaseMaterial3D, textures specified in an OmniLight3D or SpotLight3D's **Projector** property are not detected as used in 3D. This means VRAM compression is not used, which wastes memory for high-resolution textures.

**Note:** [Projector rendering is currently broken](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/59488), but 3D detection can still be fixed in the meantime.

### Steps to reproduce

- Add a MeshInstance3D node with a BoxMesh (to see the lights affecting it).
- Add a OmniLight3D node and enable shadows on it.
- Specify a projector texture in the OmniLight3D properties.
- Add a SpotLight3D node and enable shadows on it.
- Specify a projector texture in the OmniLight3D properties.

### Minimal reproduction project

[test_projector_detect_3d.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/8900218/test_projector_detect_3d.zip)

review_comments: Is it correct to assume here that the roughness channel is always green? It's always an ORM texture.
It should be fine here, yes. The Decal node does not support separate occlusion/roughness/metallic textures (and if you were to use grayscale, all channels are identical anyway).

After the automatic reimport caused by detection, the texture path in RS was not being set, so the roughness texture detection, which relies on the normal texture's path, failed.

Reimport doesn't cause a call to `Resource.set_path()` (which would also set the RS texture path) because the path doesn't change, however this state is invalidated. It should makes sense then to set it here, probably for all texture types, not just `CompressedTexture2D`, unless there is somewhere better.
